[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like SPY on 2020-03-16, the median 5-session forward return was 1.36%. The distribution is wide and left-skewed, with a standard deviation of 12.32% and a 10th percentile of -22.12%, meaning that while the typical outcome was slightly positive, severe drawdowns were common in this neighborhood.

[state]
The engine retrieved these analogs because the query state sits at extreme z-scores across nearly every feature: the 5-session return is -12.54% (z=-3), the 20-session return is -28.95% (z=-3), 20-session realised volatility is 78.3% (z=3), the drawdown from the 60-session peak is -29.11% (z=-3), and the VIX level is 82.69 (z=3). Mean absolute overnight gaps over 20 sessions are 2.78% (z=3) and dollar volume is at a 15.408 z-score regime. WTI crude fell -44.34% over 20 days and the trade-weighted USD rose 3.88%. Market sentiment registers as Greed with a value of 70. Contextual headlines from CNBC Markets note that "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and "Surging Treasury yields don’t signal a U.S. 'fiscal apocalypse' — yet." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of -2.3% and a median of 1.36%. The spread runs from -40.53% to 19.93%, with a skew of -1.141. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The 10th percentile is -22.12% and the 90th percentile is 9.37%. The bad tail is dominated by early-March 2020 industrial and energy names: Boeing (BA) on 2020-03-05 returned -40.53%, ConocoPhillips (COP) on 2020-03-04 returned -34.13%, Morgan Stanley (MS) on 2020-03-05 returned -26.49%, and the Energy Select ETF (XLE) on 2020-03-06 returned -24.26%. By contrast, Technology and Industrials names from late 2018 and mid 2019, such as AMD on 2018-12-07 (2.26%) and GE Aerospace (GE) on 2019-08-15 (2.25%), populated the positive side.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be un-holdable intra-horizon. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -4.21%, while the 10th percentile of adverse excursion reached -22.87%. The median max favourable excursion was 4.68%, with a 90th percentile of 11.67%. In terms of breach probabilities, 48% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown, 30% breached 10%, 18% breached 15%, and 14% breached 20%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on excursions is 1.11.

[stress]
Of the 14 scenarios run, 5 were skipped because their windows ended after the 5-session embargo before 2020-03-16: the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, the 2022 inflation/rate bear, the 2023-03 regional bank stress, the 2024-08-05 carry unwind, and the 2025-04 tariff shock. Among the executed scenarios, the earnings-day shock worsened the picture most, dropping the median to 0.06% (a delta of -1.3% versus baseline); its caveat notes that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The FOMC decision day scenario produced a median of -0.52% (delta -1.88%), carrying the caveat that only 92 decision days exist in the calendar so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue produced a median of 0.96% (delta -0.4%), with the caveat that blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count—a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution—and that a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. The volatility spike scenario actually improved the median to 1.87% (delta 0.51%), but its 10th percentile widened to -20.12%; its caveat states that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yielded a median of 0.89% (delta -0.47%), with the caveat that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the volatility spike, because the query VIX is 82.69 (z=3) and the scenario's 50 analogs show a 30% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; the liquidity air pocket, because the query gap20 is 2.78% (z=3) and the scenario matches the baseline median of 1.36% exactly while showing a 10th percentile of -22.12%; and the earnings-day shock, because it produces the lowest median (0.06%) among the non-skipped event shocks despite 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions,
